237393232_b75d4d85.text: Capitalizing on a well-characterized model of ELA, we examined here the ELA-induced changes in gene expression profiles of stress-sensitive CRH-neurons in the hypothalamic paraventricular nucleus (PVN) of male mice. Given the known heterogeneity of these neuronal populations, we employed single-cell RNA sequencing (RNA-seq) approaches. The use of single-cell transcriptomics identified distinct CRH-expressing neuronal populations characterized by both their gene expression repertoire and their neurotransmitter profiles

237393232_7fc15258.text: . We found no evidence for a distinction in expression patterns among cells according to ELA history, but rather observed five distinct clusters comprised of neurons from both CTL and ELA groups. Differentially expressed genes among these five clusters suggested broad distinctions among clusters based on, for example, glutamatergic versus GABAergic molecular signatures. Specifically, cluster 1 cells preferentially expressed Avp and steroid hormone receptors, cluster 2 GABAergic and neurotensinergic neurons, cluster 4 Ntng1-positive glutamatergic cells, and cluster 5 expressed arginine vasopressin (AVP), or steroid hormone receptors

237393232_d3cd021e.text: . To determine if the distribution of glutamatergic and GABAergic Crh+ neurons corresponded to prior descriptions of PVN topography, we performed immunohistochemistry for CRH-tdTomato and in situ hybridization for Slc17a6 and Gad2. Although the entire population of tdTomato+ cells were distributed throughout the PVN, cells co-expressing Crh and Slc17a6 were concentrated in the dorsal parvocellular subdivision of the PVN while Crh and Gad2-expressing cells were sparse and were found without obvious spatial pattern. Within glutamatergic CRH+ neurons, our analyses revealed two distinct populations based on Avp or Ntng1 expression. We found that CRH-AVP neurons were distributed sparsely throughout the PVN, whereas CRH-Ntng1 neurons were concentrated in the middle region of the PVN

237393232_ea63d46d.text: . In all, these findings indicate considerable heterogeneity among neonatal PVN CRH-expressing neurons according to neurotransmitter type, molecular features and location. ELA augmented the number and extent of differentially enriched genes selectively in glutamatergic Crh+ cells, with changes specific to one glutamatergic neuronal phenotype.
